result.title: A Study on Performance Enhancement of a Webcam-Based Real-Time Eye-Tracking System
result.summary: This study proposes a real-time gaze-tracking system that uses a standard RGB webcam to estimate screen coordinates. The system combines ETH-XGaze-based gaze estimation with nine-point calibration and polynomial ridge regression. To reduce errors caused by changes in head position, it also applies a conditional residual correction derived from head and pose features extracted with RTMPose. Whether this correction is used depends on the reliability of the detected features and the characteristics of the calibration data. In a preliminary experiment, one participant completed trials at 12 screen targets. The resulting mean screen-coordinate error was 204.24 pixels, which was 35.83% lower than that of xgaze-js and 57.69% lower than that of gaze_tracker. The system produced valid gaze estimates for all 12 targets. These preliminary findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining user-specific calibration with conditional pose-based correction for webcam gaze tracking. Because the evaluation involved only one participant, further experiments with more participants and a wider range of postures are required.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建了一个基于普通 RGB 摄像头的实时视线追踪系统，结合 ETH-XGaze 视线估计、九点校准与多项式岭回归，并用 RTMPose 提取的头姿特征做条件性残差修正以降低头部移动误差；单名被试的初步实验中 12 个屏幕目标的平均误差为 204.24 像素。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于人机接口层面的坐标估计工程工作，未涉及推理状态、视觉证据筛选或停止决策等机制；「人类注视位置可作为注意力信号」与视觉证据选择只有非常松散的联想，且无可用模型或数据线索，故不入选。
